🎬 CineMatch: Advanced Movie Recommendation System

🎯 Intelligent Movie Discovery Platform

🎯 Project Overview:

CineMatch is a sophisticated content-based movie recommendation system that leverages machine learning and natural language processing to deliver personalized movie suggestions. This comprehensive analysis demonstrates the complete data science pipeline from raw data exploration to production-ready deployment.

🎪 What This Project Delivers:

  • 🤖 Intelligent Recommendation Engine: Custom TF-IDF implementation with cosine similarity
  • 📊 Comprehensive EDA: Professional visualizations and statistical analysis
  • 🎨 Interactive Dashboard: Beautiful charts revealing industry insights
  • 🚀 Production Ready: Streamlit web application with TMDb API integration
  • 📈 Performance Metrics: Quantitative evaluation with similarity scoring

📖 About the Dataset:

🎥 TMDb 5000 Movies Dataset

This analysis utilizes The Movie Database (TMDb) dataset containing 5,000 movies with comprehensive metadata including:

  • 📝 Content Features: Plot summaries, genres, keywords, cast, crew
  • 💰 Financial Data: Budget, revenue, profitability metrics
  • ⭐ Quality Metrics: User ratings, vote counts, popularity scores
  • 🏢 Production Info: Companies, countries, release dates

🎯 Business Objectives:

  1. Predict Movie Success: Can we identify factors that determine commercial and critical success?
  2. Content Similarity: How accurately can we match movies based on content features?
  3. Industry Insights: What patterns exist in movie production, genres, and financial performance?
  4. Recommendation Quality: How effectively can we suggest relevant movies to users?

🚀 Project Methodology:

  • Phase 1: Data Exploration & Cleaning 📊 - Comprehensive statistical analysis and missing value treatment
  • Phase 2: Exploratory Data Analysis 🔍 - Visual exploration of key relationships and patterns
  • Phase 3: Feature Engineering ⚙️ - Text preprocessing and feature extraction
  • Phase 4: Machine Learning 🤖 - Custom algorithm implementation and optimization
  • Phase 5: Model Evaluation 📈 - Performance testing and validation
  • Phase 6: Production Deployment 🚀 - Streamlit web application development

    df_credits = pd.read_csv('Dataset/tmdb_5000_credits.csv')
    print(f"✅ Movies dataset loaded: {df_movies.shape}")

🔍 SECTION 3: DATA QUALITY ASSESSMENT & STATISTICAL OVERVIEW

🎯 Quality Assessment Goals:

Conduct comprehensive data quality analysis to ensure reliable foundations for our recommendation system. This section performs statistical validation, identifies data inconsistencies, and establishes data integrity standards for subsequent analysis phases.

📊 Statistical Analysis Components:

  • 📈 Descriptive Statistics: Comprehensive statistical summaries for all numerical features
  • 🔍 Missing Value Analysis: Detailed assessment of null values and data completeness
  • 📊 Data Distribution Analysis: Understanding value distributions and identifying outliers
  • 🎯 Data Type Validation: Ensuring proper data types and format consistency

🔬 Quality Metrics:

  • ✅ Data Completeness: Percentage of non-null values across all features
  • 📊 Value Consistency: Checking for logical consistency and valid ranges
  • 🎬 Domain Validation: Movie-specific validation rules and constraints
  • 🔗 Relationship Integrity: Validating connections between datasets

🛠️ Data Cleaning Preparation:

  • 🚨 Issue Identification: Cataloging data quality problems and anomalies
  • 📋 Cleaning Strategy: Developing targeted approaches for each data issue

  • 📈 Quality Improvements: Quantifying data enhancement opportunities

# 🧹 STEP 1: CRITICAL MISSING VALUES TREATMENT

print("🧹 Starting Data Cleaning Process...")
print("=" * 50)

# Check initial dataset shape
initial_rows = len(df)
print(f"📊 Initial dataset size: {initial_rows:,} rows")

# Define critical columns for recommendation system
critical_columns = ['overview', 'genres', 'keywords', 'cast', 'crew']

print(f"\n🔍 Checking critical columns: {critical_columns}")
for col in critical_columns:
    missing_count = df[col].isnull().sum()
    missing_pct = (missing_count / len(df)) * 100
    print(f"   {col}: {missing_count} missing ({missing_pct:.1f}%)")

# Remove rows with missing critical columns
df_clean = df.dropna(subset=critical_columns)
dropped_rows = initial_rows - len(df_clean)

print(f"\n✅ Removed {dropped_rows:,} rows with missing critical data")
print(f"📊 Cleaned dataset size: {len(df_clean):,} rows")
print(f"📉 Data retention: {(len(df_clean)/initial_rows)*100:.1f}%")

# Update main dataframe
df = df_clean.copy()
print("\n✅ Critical missing values treatment completed!")
print("=" * 50)

# 🧹 STEP 2: DUPLICATE REMOVAL & DATA VALIDATION

print("🔍 Checking for duplicate entries...")
print("=" * 50)

# Check for duplicates
initial_count = len(df)
duplicate_count = df.duplicated().sum()
print(f"🔍 Duplicate rows found: {duplicate_count}")

if duplicate_count > 0:
    # Remove duplicates
    df = df.drop_duplicates()
    removed = initial_count - len(df)
    print(f"✅ Removed {removed:,} duplicate rows")
else:
    print("✅ No duplicate rows found!")

# Check for duplicate titles (potential data quality issue)
title_duplicates = df['title'].duplicated().sum()
print(f"🎬 Duplicate movie titles: {title_duplicates}")

if title_duplicates > 0:
    print("⚠️  Movies with duplicate titles:")
    duplicate_titles = df[df['title'].duplicated(keep=False)]['title'].unique()
    for title in duplicate_titles[:5]:  # Show first 5
        print(f"   - {title}")

print(f"\n📊 Final dataset size after cleaning: {len(df):,} rows")
print("✅ Duplicate removal completed!")
print("=" * 50)

# 🧹 STEP 3: FINANCIAL DATA CLEANING & VALIDATION

print("💰 Cleaning Financial Data (Budget & Revenue)...")
print("=" * 50)

# Analyze zero values in financial columns
budget_zeros = (df['budget'] == 0).sum()
revenue_zeros = (df['revenue'] == 0).sum()

print(f"💸 Budget = 0: {budget_zeros:,} rows ({budget_zeros/len(df)*100:.1f}%)")
print(f"💰 Revenue = 0: {revenue_zeros:,} rows ({revenue_zeros/len(df)*100:.1f}%)")

# Convert zeros to NaN for proper statistical analysis
# (Zero likely represents missing data, not actual zero budget/revenue)
df['budget'] = df['budget'].replace(0, np.nan)
df['revenue'] = df['revenue'].replace(0, np.nan)

# Calculate basic financial statistics
budget_stats = df['budget'].describe()
revenue_stats = df['revenue'].describe()

print(f"\n📊 BUDGET STATISTICS (non-zero values):")
print(f"   Count: {budget_stats['count']:,.0f}")
print(f"   Mean: ${budget_stats['mean']:,.0f}")
print(f"   Median: ${budget_stats['50%']:,.0f}")
print(f"   Max: ${budget_stats['max']:,.0f}")

print(f"\n📊 REVENUE STATISTICS (non-zero values):")
print(f"   Count: {revenue_stats['count']:,.0f}")
print(f"   Mean: ${revenue_stats['mean']:,.0f}")
print(f"   Median: ${revenue_stats['50%']:,.0f}")
print(f"   Max: ${revenue_stats['max']:,.0f}")

# Calculate profitability metrics for available data
valid_financial = df.dropna(subset=['budget', 'revenue'])
if len(valid_financial) > 0:
    valid_financial['profit'] = valid_financial['revenue'] - valid_financial['budget']
    valid_financial['roi'] = (valid_financial['revenue'] / valid_financial['budget']) * 100
    
    profitable_count = (valid_financial['profit'] > 0).sum()
    print(f"\n💹 PROFITABILITY ANALYSIS:")
    print(f"   Movies with financial data: {len(valid_financial):,}")
    print(f"   Profitable movies: {profitable_count:,} ({profitable_count/len(valid_financial)*100:.1f}%)")
    print(f"   Average ROI: {valid_financial['roi'].mean():.1f}%")

print("\n✅ Financial data cleaning completed!")
print("=" * 50)

# 📈 SECTION 5: DISTRIBUTION ANALYSIS & KEY METRICS

print("📈 Analyzing Key Feature Distributions...")
print("=" * 60)

# Create comprehensive distribution analysis
fig, ((ax1, ax2), (ax3, ax4)) = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(20, 16))
fig.suptitle('📊 KEY FEATURE DISTRIBUTIONS ANALYSIS', fontsize=20, fontweight='bold', y=0.98)

# 1. Movie Ratings Distribution
ax1.hist(df['vote_average'], bins=30, alpha=0.7, color='skyblue', edgecolor='navy', linewidth=1)
ax1.axvline(df['vote_average'].mean(), color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, 
           label=f'Mean: {df["vote_average"].mean():.2f}')
ax1.axvline(df['vote_average'].median(), color='orange', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, 
           label=f'Median: {df["vote_average"].median():.2f}')
ax1.set_title('⭐ Movie Ratings Distribution', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
ax1.set_xlabel('Vote Average', fontsize=12)
ax1.set_ylabel('Number of Movies', fontsize=12)
ax1.legend()
ax1.grid(alpha=0.3)

# 2. Release Year Distribution
df['release_year'] = pd.to_datetime(df['release_date'], errors='coerce').dt.year
year_counts = df['release_year'].value_counts().sort_index()
year_counts = year_counts[year_counts.index >= 1980]  # Focus on modern cinema

ax2.plot(year_counts.index, year_counts.values, linewidth=3, color='green', marker='o', markersize=4)
ax2.fill_between(year_counts.index, year_counts.values, alpha=0.3, color='lightgreen')
ax2.set_title('📅 Movie Production Timeline', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
ax2.set_xlabel('Release Year', fontsize=12)
ax2.set_ylabel('Number of Movies', fontsize=12)
ax2.grid(alpha=0.3)

# 3. Budget Distribution (log scale for better visualization)
budget_clean = df[df['budget'] > 0]['budget']
ax3.hist(np.log10(budget_clean), bins=30, alpha=0.7, color='gold', edgecolor='orange', linewidth=1)
ax3.set_title('💰 Budget Distribution (Log Scale)', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
ax3.set_xlabel('Log10(Budget)', fontsize=12)
ax3.set_ylabel('Number of Movies', fontsize=12)
ax3.grid(alpha=0.3)

# Add budget categories
budget_labels = ['$1K', '$10K', '$100K', '$1M', '$10M', '$100M', '$1B']
budget_ticks = [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9]
ax3.set_xticks(budget_ticks)
ax3.set_xticklabels(budget_labels)

# 4. Popularity vs Rating Scatter

# 💰 ENHANCED BUDGET VS REVENUE ANALYSIS
print("💰 Creating Enhanced Budget vs Revenue Visualization")

# Load original dataset for financial analysis
movies_financial = pd.read_csv('Dataset/tmdb_5000_movies.csv')

# Clean and filter the data
financial_clean = movies_financial[(movies_financial['budget'] > 0) & 
                                  (movies_financial['revenue'] > 0) & 
                                  (movies_financial['vote_average'] > 0)]

# Remove extreme outliers (top 2% to focus on main distribution)
budget_q98 = financial_clean['budget'].quantile(0.98)
revenue_q98 = financial_clean['revenue'].quantile(0.98)
financial_clean = financial_clean[(financial_clean['budget'] <= budget_q98) & 
                                 (financial_clean['revenue'] <= revenue_q98)]

# Convert to millions for better readability
financial_clean['budget_millions'] = financial_clean['budget'] / 1e6
financial_clean['revenue_millions'] = financial_clean['revenue'] / 1e6
financial_clean['profit_millions'] = financial_clean['revenue_millions'] - financial_clean['budget_millions']
financial_clean['roi'] = (financial_clean['revenue'] / financial_clean['budget']) * 100

# Create enhanced visualization
fig, ((ax1, ax2), (ax3, ax4)) = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(20, 16))
fig.suptitle('💰 COMPREHENSIVE BUDGET vs REVENUE ANALYSIS', fontsize=20, fontweight='bold', y=0.98)

# 1. Enhanced Scatter Plot with Rating Colors
scatter1 = ax1.scatter(financial_clean['budget_millions'], 
                      financial_clean['revenue_millions'],
                      c=financial_clean['vote_average'], 
                      cmap='RdYlBu_r', 
                      s=60, 
                      alpha=0.7, 
                      edgecolors='black', 
                      linewidth=0.5)

# Add trend line
z = np.polyfit(financial_clean['budget_millions'], financial_clean['revenue_millions'], 1)
p = np.poly1d(z)
trend_x = np.linspace(financial_clean['budget_millions'].min(), 
                     financial_clean['budget_millions'].max(), 100)
ax1.plot(trend_x, p(trend_x), "r--", alpha=0.8, linewidth=3, 
         label=f'Trend: y = {z[0]:.1f}x + {z[1]:.1f}')

# Calculate and display correlation
correlation = financial_clean['budget_millions'].corr(financial_clean['revenue_millions'])
ax1.text(0.05, 0.95, f'Correlation: {correlation:.3f}', 
         transform=ax1.transAxes, fontsize=12, fontweight='bold',
         bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.3", facecolor="white", alpha=0.8))

ax1.set_title('🎬 Budget vs Revenue by Rating', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
ax1.set_xlabel('Budget (Millions USD)', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_ylabel('Revenue (Millions USD)', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax1.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
ax1.legend(fontsize=12)

# Add colorbar
cbar1 = plt.colorbar(scatter1, ax=ax1)
cbar1.set_label('Movie Rating', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# 2. ROI Distribution
roi_data = financial_clean['roi'].clip(upper=500)  # Cap extreme ROI values
n, bins, patches = ax2.hist(roi_data, bins=30, alpha=0.7, edgecolor='black', linewidth=1)

# Color gradient for histogram
colors = plt.cm.viridis(np.linspace(0, 1, len(patches)))
for patch, color in zip(patches, colors):
    patch.set_facecolor(color)

def extract_keywords(text):
    """Extract keyword names from JSON string"""
    try:
        return ' '.join([item['name'] for item in ast.literal_eval(text)])
    except:
        return ''

# Process keywords data

print(f"✅ Extracted {len(keyword_list):,} total keywords")
print(f"📊 Unique keywords: {len(set(keyword_list)):,}")

# Create word frequency analysis
keyword_counts = Counter(keyword_list)
top_keywords = dict(keyword_counts.most_common(20))

print(f"\n🏆 TOP 10 MOST COMMON KEYWORDS:")
print("-" * 40)
for i, (keyword, count) in enumerate(list(top_keywords.items())[:10], 1):
    print(f"{i:2d}. {keyword:<20} ({count:,} movies)")

        wordcloud = WordCloud(
            width=800, height=400,

🧹 SECTION 4: DATA PREPROCESSING & CLEANING

🎯 Preprocessing Objectives:

Transform raw movie data into clean, structured format suitable for machine learning. This includes parsing JSON fields, extracting meaningful features, and creating unified text representations.

🔧 Data Transformation Pipeline:

  • 🎭 Genre Extraction: Parse JSON genre data into clean categorical features
  • 🎬 Cast Processing: Extract top 3 cast members from nested JSON structures
  • 🎪 Keyword Cleaning: Process movie keywords and themes from JSON format
  • 🎯 Director Identification: Extract director information from crew data
  • 📝 Text Normalization: Clean and standardize text features for analysis

🎨 Feature Combination Strategy:

  • 🔄 Multi-Source Integration: Combine plot + genres + cast + keywords + director
  • 📝 Text Normalization: Stemming, lowercasing, space removal
  • ⚖️ Feature Weighting: Balance different feature types for optimal similarity
  • 🎯 Quality Assurance: Validate feature extraction and consistency

# Extract director
def fetch_director(text):
    try:
        for item in ast.literal_eval(text):
            if item['job'] == 'Director':
                return [item['name']]
        return []
    except:
        return []

# 🤖 CUSTOM ML IMPLEMENTATION: TF-IDF & COSINE SIMILARITY

print("🤖 Implementing Custom Machine Learning Pipeline...")
print("=" * 70)

# Import required libraries for custom implementation
from collections import Counter
import math

def create_vocabulary(documents, max_features=5000):
    """
    Create vocabulary from document collection with intelligent filtering
    
    Args:
        documents: List of text documents
        max_features: Maximum vocabulary size
    
    Returns:
        List of most important words for vectorization
    """
    print(f"📚 Building vocabulary from {len(documents):,} documents...")
    
    # Enhanced stop words for movie domain
    stop_words = {
        'the', 'a', 'an', 'and', 'or', 'but', 'in', 'on', 'at', 'to', 'for', 
        'of', 'with', 'by', 'is', 'are', 'was', 'were', 'be', 'been', 'have', 
        'has', 'had', 'do', 'does', 'did', 'will', 'would', 'could', 'should', 
        'may', 'might', 'must', 'can', 'this', 'that', 'these', 'those', 
        'i', 'you', 'he', 'she', 'it', 'we', 'they', 'me', 'him', 'her', 'us', 'them'
    }
    
    word_counts = Counter()
    
    # Process documents and count word frequencies
    for doc in documents:
        words = [word for word in doc.split() 
                if word not in stop_words and len(word) > 2]
        word_counts.update(words)
    
    # Get top words by frequency
    vocab = [word for word, count in word_counts.most_common(max_features)]
    
    print(f"✅ Vocabulary created: {len(vocab):,} terms")
    print(f"📊 Total unique words: {len(word_counts):,}")
    print(f"🎯 Vocabulary coverage: {len(vocab)/len(word_counts)*100:.1f}%")
    
    return vocab

def compute_tf_idf(documents, vocabulary):
    """
    Compute TF-IDF matrix using custom implementation
    
    Args:
        documents: List of text documents
        vocabulary: Word vocabulary for vectorization
    
    Returns:
        NumPy array representing TF-IDF matrix
    """
    print(f"🧮 Computing TF-IDF matrix...")
    
    N = len(documents)
    tfidf_matrix = []
    
    # Compute document frequency for each vocabulary word
    print("   📊 Calculating document frequencies...")
    df = {}
    for word in vocabulary:
        df[word] = sum(1 for doc in documents if word in doc.split())
    
    # Process each document
    print("   🔄 Processing documents...")
    for i, doc in enumerate(documents):
        if (i + 1) % 1000 == 0:
            print(f"      Progress: {i+1:,}/{N:,} documents")
            
        words = doc.split()
        word_count = Counter(words)
        doc_length = len(words)
        
        tfidf_vector = []
        for word in vocabulary:
            # Calculate TF (Term Frequency)
            tf = word_count[word] / doc_length if doc_length > 0 else 0
            
            # Calculate IDF (Inverse Document Frequency)
            idf = math.log(N / (df[word] + 1))  # +1 to avoid division by zero
            
            # TF-IDF score
            tfidf_vector.append(tf * idf)
        
        tfidf_matrix.append(tfidf_vector)
    
    matrix = np.array(tfidf_matrix)
    print(f"✅ TF-IDF matrix computed: {matrix.shape}")
    
    return matrix

def cosine_similarity_matrix(matrix):
    """
    Compute cosine similarity matrix efficiently
    
    Args:
        matrix: TF-IDF matrix
    
    Returns:
        Cosine similarity matrix
    """
    print(f"📊 Computing cosine similarity matrix...")
    
    # Normalize vectors to unit length
    norms = np.linalg.norm(matrix, axis=1, keepdims=True)
    norms[norms == 0] = 1  # Avoid division by zero
    normalized = matrix / norms
    
    # Compute similarity matrix using dot product
    similarity_matrix = np.dot(normalized, normalized.T)
    
    print(f"✅ Similarity matrix computed: {similarity_matrix.shape}")
    
    return similarity_matrix

# Execute the complete ML pipeline
print("🚀 Starting Custom ML Pipeline Execution...")
print("-" * 70)

# Step 1: Create vocabulary
vocabulary = create_vocabulary(df['tags'].values, max_features=5000)

# Step 2: Compute TF-IDF matrix
tfidf_matrix = compute_tf_idf(df['tags'].values, vocabulary)

# Step 3: Compute similarity matrix
similarity = cosine_similarity_matrix(tfidf_matrix)

# Pipeline completion summary
print("\n🎉 MACHINE LEARNING PIPELINE COMPLETED!")
print("=" * 70)
print(f"📚 Vocabulary Size: {len(vocabulary):,} unique terms")
print(f"📊 TF-IDF Matrix: {tfidf_matrix.shape} (movies × features)")
print(f"🔗 Similarity Matrix: {similarity.shape} (movies × movies)")
print(f"💾 Memory Usage: {(tfidf_matrix.nbytes + similarity.nbytes) / 1024**2:.1f} MB")
print(f"🎯 Similarity Range: [{similarity.min():.3f}, {similarity.max():.3f}]")
print("=" * 70)

# 📈 RECOMMENDATION SYSTEM TESTING & VALIDATION

print("🧪 Starting Comprehensive Recommendation System Testing...")
print("=" * 70)

def recommend_movies(movie_title, num_recommendations=5, show_details=True):
    """
    Generate movie recommendations with detailed analysis
    
    Args:
        movie_title: Input movie for recommendation
        num_recommendations: Number of recommendations to return
        show_details: Whether to display detailed information
    
    Returns:
        List of recommended movies with similarity scores
    """
    try:
        # Find movie index
        movie_index = df[df['title'] == movie_title].index[0]
        
        # Get similarity scores for this movie
        similarity_scores = similarity[movie_index]
        
        # Sort movies by similarity (excluding the movie itself)
        movie_similarities = list(enumerate(similarity_scores))
        movie_similarities = sorted(movie_similarities, reverse=True, key=lambda x: x[1])
        
        # Get top recommendations (skip first one as it's the movie itself)
        top_movies = movie_similarities[1:num_recommendations+1]
        
        recommendations = []
        
        if show_details:
            print(f"\n🎬 RECOMMENDATIONS FOR: '{movie_title}'")
            print("-" * 60)
            
        for i, (movie_idx, similarity_score) in enumerate(top_movies, 1):
            rec_title = df.iloc[movie_idx]['title']
            recommendations.append({
                'rank': i,
                'title': rec_title,
                'similarity_score': similarity_score,
                'movie_id': df.iloc[movie_idx]['movie_id']
            })
            
            if show_details:
                print(f"{i}. {rec_title:<50} (Similarity: {similarity_score:.3f})")
        
        return recommendations
        
    except IndexError:
        print(f"❌ Movie '{movie_title}' not found in dataset!")
        return []
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"❌ Error generating recommendations: {str(e)}")
        return []

# Test the recommendation system
print("🎯 Testing Recommendation System with Sample Movie...")

# Single movie test
test_movie = "The Dark Knight Rises"
recommendations = recommend_movies(test_movie, num_recommendations=5)

if recommendations:
    print(f"\n✅ Successfully generated {len(recommendations)} recommendations!")
    
    # Calculate recommendation quality metrics
    similarity_scores = [rec['similarity_score'] for rec in recommendations]
    avg_similarity = np.mean(similarity_scores)
    similarity_std = np.std(similarity_scores)
    
    print(f"\n📊 RECOMMENDATION QUALITY METRICS:")
    print("-" * 50)
    print(f"🎯 Average Similarity: {avg_similarity:.3f}")
    print(f"📏 Similarity Range: {min(similarity_scores):.3f} - {max(similarity_scores):.3f}")
    print(f"📊 Standard Deviation: {similarity_std:.3f}")
    print(f"🎪 Consistency Score: {(1 - similarity_std) * 100:.1f}%")

print("\n✅ Initial recommendation testing completed!")
print("=" * 70)

print("🎪 Conducting Comprehensive Multi-Movie Testing...")

# Diverse test movie selection covering different genres and eras
test_movies = [
    'Avatar',                    # Sci-Fi Blockbuster
    'The Dark Knight Rises',     # Superhero/Action

    'Toy Story',                 # Animated Family
    'The Godfather'              # Classic Drama
]

print("🎬 TEST MOVIE PORTFOLIO:")
print("-" * 40)
for i, movie in enumerate(test_movies, 1):
    print(f"{i}. {movie}")

# Comprehensive testing with detailed analysis
all_test_results = {}
performance_metrics = []

for movie in test_movies:
    print(f"\n{'='*20} TESTING: {movie} {'='*20}")
    
    recommendations = recommend_movies(movie, num_recommendations=5, show_details=True)
    
    if recommendations:
        # Store results
        all_test_results[movie] = recommendations
        
        # Calculate metrics
        similarities = [rec['similarity_score'] for rec in recommendations]
        metrics = {
            'movie': movie,
            'avg_similarity': np.mean(similarities),
            'max_similarity': max(similarities),
            'min_similarity': min(similarities),
            'similarity_range': max(similarities) - min(similarities),
            'consistency': (1 - np.std(similarities)) * 100
        }
        performance_metrics.append(metrics)
        
        print(f"\n📊 Performance: Avg={metrics['avg_similarity']:.3f}, "
              f"Range={metrics['similarity_range']:.3f}, "
              f"Consistency={metrics['consistency']:.1f}%")
    else:
        print(f"❌ Testing failed for {movie}")

# Overall system performance analysis

colors = plt.cm.Set3(np.linspace(0, 1, len(top_genres)))
wedges, texts, autotexts = ax1.pie(top_genres.values, labels=top_genres.index, autopct='%1.1f%%', 
                                   colors=colors, startangle=90, explode=[0.05]*len(top_genres))
ax1.set_title('🎬 Top Movie Genres Distribution', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
# Make percentage text bold
for autotext in autotexts:
    autotext.set_color('white')
    autotext.set_fontweight('bold')
    autotext.set_fontsize(10)

# 2. Genre vs Rating Analysis (Top Middle)
ax2 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 2)
genre_ratings = []
genre_names = []
for genre in genre_counts.head(10).index:
    genre_movies = movies_df[movies_df['genre_list'].apply(lambda x: genre in x)]
    if len(genre_movies) > 10:  # Only genres with sufficient data
        genre_ratings.append(genre_movies['vote_average'].values)
        genre_names.append(genre)

bp = ax2.boxplot(genre_ratings, labels=genre_names, patch_artist=True)
colors = plt.cm.viridis(np.linspace(0, 1, len(bp['boxes'])))
for patch, color in zip(bp['boxes'], colors):
    patch.set_facecolor(color)
    patch.set_alpha(0.7)
ax2.set_title('📊 Genre vs Rating Distribution', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
ax2.set_ylabel('Movie Rating', fontsize=12)
ax2.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
ax2.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

# 3. Revenue by Genre (Top Right)
ax3 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 3)
genre_revenue = {}
for genre in genre_counts.head(8).index:
    genre_movies = movies_df[movies_df['genre_list'].apply(lambda x: genre in x)]
    avg_revenue = genre_movies['revenue'].replace(0, np.nan).mean() / 1e6  # Convert to millions
    if not np.isnan(avg_revenue):
        genre_revenue[genre] = avg_revenue

genre_rev_df = pd.DataFrame(list(genre_revenue.items()), columns=['Genre', 'Avg_Revenue'])
genre_rev_df = genre_rev_df.sort_values('Avg_Revenue', ascending=True)

bars = ax3.barh(genre_rev_df['Genre'], genre_rev_df['Avg_Revenue'], 
                color=plt.cm.plasma(np.linspace(0, 1, len(genre_rev_df))))
ax3.set_title('💰 Average Revenue by Genre', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
ax3.set_xlabel('Average Revenue (Millions USD)', fontsize=12)
ax3.grid(axis='x', alpha=0.3)
# Add value labels
for bar in bars:
    width = bar.get_width()
    ax3.text(width + 1, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height()/2, 
             f'${width:.1f}M', ha='left', va='center', fontweight='bold')

# 4. Decade Analysis (Bottom Left)
ax4 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 4)
movies_df['release_year'] = pd.to_datetime(movies_df['release_date'], errors='coerce').dt.year
movies_df['decade'] = (movies_df['release_year'] // 10) * 10

decade_counts = movies_df['decade'].value_counts().sort_index()
decade_counts = decade_counts[decade_counts.index >= 1980]  # Focus on modern cinema

bars4 = ax4.bar(decade_counts.index, decade_counts.values, 
                color=plt.cm.coolwarm(np.linspace(0, 1, len(decade_counts))), 
                alpha=0.8, edgecolor='black', linewidth=1)
ax4.set_title('📅 Movies by Decade', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
ax4.set_xlabel('Decade', fontsize=12)
ax4.set_ylabel('Number of Movies', fontsize=12)
ax4.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)
# Add value labels
for bar in bars4:
    height = bar.get_height()
    ax4.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2, height + 5, 
             f'{int(height)}', ha='center', va='bottom', fontweight='bold')

# 5. Budget vs Revenue Correlation (Bottom Middle)
ax5 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 5)
# Filter out zero values and outliers
budget_revenue_df = movies_df[(movies_df['budget'] > 0) & (movies_df['revenue'] > 0)]
budget_revenue_df = budget_revenue_df[budget_revenue_df['budget'] < budget_revenue_df['budget'].quantile(0.95)]

scatter = ax5.scatter(budget_revenue_df['budget']/1e6, budget_revenue_df['revenue']/1e6, 
                     c=budget_revenue_df['vote_average'], cmap='RdYlBu_r', 
                     alpha=0.6, s=30, edgecolors='black', linewidth=0.5)
ax5.set_title('💸 Budget vs Revenue Analysis', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
ax5.set_xlabel('Budget (Millions USD)', fontsize=12)
ax5.set_ylabel('Revenue (Millions USD)', fontsize=12)
ax5.grid(alpha=0.3)

# Add colorbar
cbar = plt.colorbar(scatter, ax=ax5)
cbar.set_label('Movie Rating', fontsize=12)

# Add trend line
z = np.polyfit(budget_revenue_df['budget']/1e6, budget_revenue_df['revenue']/1e6, 1)
p = np.poly1d(z)
ax5.plot(budget_revenue_df['budget']/1e6, p(budget_revenue_df['budget']/1e6), 
         "r--", alpha=0.8, linewidth=2, label=f'Trend: y={z[0]:.1f}x+{z[1]:.1f}')
ax5.legend()

# 6. Runtime Distribution (Bottom Right)
ax6 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 6)
runtime_data = movies_df['runtime'].dropna()
runtime_data = runtime_data[(runtime_data > 60) & (runtime_data < 200)]  # Filter reasonable values

n, bins, patches = ax6.hist(runtime_data, bins=25, alpha=0.7, edgecolor='black', linewidth=1)

for i, (patch, bin_val) in enumerate(zip(patches, bins)):
    patch.set_facecolor(cm(i / len(patches)))

ax6.axvline(runtime_data.mean(), color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, 
           label=f'Mean: {runtime_data.mean():.0f} min')
ax6.axvline(runtime_data.median(), color='orange', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, 
           label=f'Median: {runtime_data.median():.0f} min')
ax6.set_title('⏱️ Movie Runtime Distribution', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
ax6.set_xlabel('Runtime (minutes)', fontsize=12)
ax6.set_ylabel('Number of Movies', fontsize=12)
ax6.legend()
ax6.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

plt.suptitle('🎬 COMPREHENSIVE MOVIE INDUSTRY ANALYSIS', fontsize=24, fontweight='bold', y=0.98)
plt.tight_layout()

# Print insights

# 🎯 BEAUTIFUL RECOMMENDATION RESULTS VISUALIZATION
print("🎬 Creating Beautiful Recommendation Showcase")

# Enhanced recommendation function with detailed results
def get_detailed_recommendations(movie_title, top_n=5):
    """Get detailed recommendations with similarity scores and metadata"""
    try:
        movie_index = df[df['title'] == movie_title].index[0]
        distances = similarity[movie_index]
        movies_list = sorted(list(enumerate(distances)), reverse=True, key=lambda x: x[1])[1:top_n+1]
        
        recommendations = []
        for i, (idx, score) in enumerate(movies_list):
            rec_title = df.iloc[idx]['title']
            recommendations.append({
                'rank': i + 1,
                'title': rec_title,
                'similarity': score,
                'movie_id': df.iloc[idx]['movie_id']
            })
        return recommendations
    except:
        return []

# Test with popular movies
test_movies = ['Avatar', 'The Dark Knight Rises', 'Inception', 'Toy Story']
all_recommendations = {}

for movie in test_movies:
    recommendations = get_detailed_recommendations(movie)
    all_recommendations[movie] = recommendations

# Create stunning visualization
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(20, 16))
fig.suptitle('🎬 CINEMATCH RECOMMENDATION SHOWCASE', fontsize=24, fontweight='bold', y=0.98)

colors = ['#FF6B6B', '#4ECDC4', '#45B7D1', '#96CEB4', '#FECCA7']

for idx, (movie, ax) in enumerate(zip(test_movies, axes.flat)):
    recommendations = all_recommendations[movie]
    
    if recommendations:
        titles = [rec['title'] for rec in recommendations]
        similarities = [rec['similarity'] for rec in recommendations]
        ranks = [rec['rank'] for rec in recommendations]
        
        # Create horizontal bar chart
        bars = ax.barh(range(len(titles)), similarities, 
                      color=[colors[i % len(colors)] for i in range(len(titles))],
                      alpha=0.8, edgecolor='black', linewidth=1.5)
        
        # Customize the chart
        ax.set_yticks(range(len(titles)))
        ax.set_yticklabels([f"{rank}. {title}" for rank, title in zip(ranks, titles)], fontsize=11)
        ax.set_xlabel('Similarity Score', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
        ax.set_title(f'🎭 Recommendations for "{movie}"', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
        ax.grid(axis='x', alpha=0.3)
        ax.set_xlim(0, max(similarities) * 1.1)
        
        # Add value labels
        for bar, similarity in zip(bars, similarities):
            width = bar.get_width()
            ax.text(width + 0.01, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height()/2, 
                   f'{similarity:.3f}', ha='left', va='center', fontweight='bold', fontsize=10)
        
        # Add movie poster placeholder (decorative element)
        ax.text(0.02, len(titles) - 0.5, '🎬', fontsize=24, ha='left', va='center', alpha=0.7)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# Create summary statistics table
print("\n📊 RECOMMENDATION SYSTEM SUMMARY STATISTICS")
print("=" * 80)

summary_stats = []
for movie, recommendations in all_recommendations.items():
    if recommendations:
        similarities = [rec['similarity'] for rec in recommendations]
        summary_stats.append({
            'Movie': movie,
            'Avg_Similarity': np.mean(similarities),
            'Max_Similarity': max(similarities),
            'Min_Similarity': min(similarities),
            'Std_Similarity': np.std(similarities)
        })

summary_df = pd.DataFrame(summary_stats)

# Beautiful table formatting

for _, row in summary_df.iterrows():

          f"{row['Min_Similarity']:<10.3f} {row['Std_Similarity']:<10.3f}")

print("=" * 80)

# Feature importance analysis
# Compute IDF scores for vocabulary words
N = len(df)
word_importance = []

for word in vocabulary[:1000]:  # Top 1000 words for visualization
    doc_freq = sum(1 for doc in df['tags'] if word in doc.split())
    idf_score = math.log(N / (doc_freq + 1))
    word_importance.append((word, idf_score, doc_freq))

# Sort by IDF score (higher = more discriminative)
word_importance.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)

# Create DataFrame for visualization
top_features = pd.DataFrame(word_importance[:20], columns=['Feature', 'IDF_Score', 'Doc_Frequency'])

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.barplot(data=top_features, x='IDF_Score', y='Feature', palette='viridis')
plt.title('Top 20 Most Discriminative Features (Highest IDF Scores)')
plt.xlabel('IDF Score (Higher = More Discriminative)')
plt.ylabel('Feature')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

print("📊 Feature Analysis:")
print(f"Total vocabulary: {len(vocabulary)} words")
print(f"Most discriminative features (rare but meaningful):")
for i, (word, idf, freq) in enumerate(word_importance[:5]):
    print(f"{i+1}. '{word}' - IDF: {idf:.3f}, appears in {freq} movies")

# 🚀 FAST PRODUCTION DEPLOYMENT SUMMARY

import pickle
import os

print("💾 Production Deployment Status...")
print("=" * 50)

# Ensure models directory exists
models_dir = 'models'
if not os.path.exists(models_dir):
    os.makedirs(models_dir)
    print(f"📁 Created models directory: {models_dir}/")

# Check if model files exist in models folder
files_to_check = [
    ('models/movie_list.pkl', 'movie_list.pkl'),
    ('models/similarity.pkl', 'similarity.pkl'), 
    ('models/tfidf_vectorizer.pkl', 'tfidf_vectorizer.pkl')
]

existing_files = []
missing_files = []

print(f"\n🔍 Checking model files in {models_dir}/ folder...")
for model_path, filename in files_to_check:
    if os.path.exists(model_path):
        size = os.path.getsize(model_path) / 1024**2
        existing_files.append((filename, size))
        print(f"✅ {filename} exists ({size:.1f} MB)")
    else:
        missing_files.append(filename)
        print(f"❌ {filename} not found in models/ folder")

# Check for old model files in root directory
root_files = []
for _, filename in files_to_check:
    if os.path.exists(filename):
        size = os.path.getsize(filename) / 1024**2
        root_files.append((filename, size))

if root_files:
    print(f"\n⚠️  Found {len(root_files)} model files in root directory:")
    for filename, size in root_files:
        print(f"   📄 {filename} ({size:.1f} MB)")
    print("💡 These should be moved to the models/ folder")

if len(existing_files) == 3:
    total_size = sum(size for _, size in existing_files)
    print(f"\n🎉 DEPLOYMENT PACKAGE READY!")
    print(f"📦 Total package size: {total_size:.1f} MB")
    print(f"✅ All required files are available in models/ folder")
    
    print(f"\n🚀 TO LAUNCH YOUR APP:")
    print("   streamlit run app.py")
    
elif len(existing_files) > 0:
    print(f"\n⚠️  Partial deployment package found")
    print(f"📂 {len(existing_files)}/3 files available in models/ folder")
    print("💡 Run the TF-IDF training cell to generate missing files")
    
else:
    print(f"\n📝 DEPLOYMENT PREPARATION NEEDED:")
    print("1. Ensure the ML pipeline has been executed")
    print("2. Verify similarity matrix is computed") 
    print("3. Run previous cells to generate model files")
    print(f"4. Models will be saved to {models_dir}/ folder")

print(f"\n✅ Deployment check completed! 🎬")

# Additional deployment information
print(f"\n📋 DEPLOYMENT REQUIREMENTS:")
print(f"- {models_dir}/movie_list.pkl (movie database)")
print(f"- {models_dir}/similarity.pkl (similarity matrix)")  
print(f"- {models_dir}/tfidf_vectorizer.pkl (model metadata)")
print("- app.py (Streamlit application)")
